completion_notes: Implementation path: hand-authored Python adapter `Algo2CodePCGSolver` mirroring the canonical PCG LaTeX line-by-line; canonical LaTeX shipped verbatim in `packages/algo2code/src/algo2code/library/pcg.py` as `PCG_ALGORITHM_LATEX` (byte-identical to `pcg_algorithm_latex.latex` in this JSON, length 1878).

Reason for hand-translation: `algo2code.expr_parser` tokenises each ASCII letter individually -> rejects multi-letter LHS like `pq` in `\State $pq = p^\top q$`. `algo2code/backends/numpy_codegen.py` is a one-line stub. Extending parser + numpy backend is out of P6-1 scope. LaTeX text preserved unmodified; the deferral is documented in `pcg.py`, in the `Algo2CodePCGSolver` class docstring, and in the test module.

pcg_algorithm_latex.description: Canonical PCG algpseudocode for algo2code → Taichi backend. Resolved 2026-04-29 after debate between for-loop (v1) and while-loop (v2) forms; v1 chosen with corrections (consistent callable preconditioner, breakdown guard, relative tolerance, 3-tuple return matching LinearSolverInterface). Mirrored in dev/design_docs/.
pcg_algorithm_latex.args_signature: A:matrix, b:vector, x:vector, apply_M_inv:callable, tol:scalar, maxiter:scalar
pcg_algorithm_latex.return_signature: (x:vector, k:scalar, r_norm:scalar) — matches LinearSolverInterface.solve return tuple[np.ndarray, int, float].
pcg_algorithm_latex.preconditioner_contract: `apply_M_inv` is a callable v -> M^{-1} v. Caller is responsible for the inversion strategy (Jacobi, ILU, AMG, identity). When constructing the adapter with `precond_fn=None`, bind apply_M_inv = lambda v: v.copy() at adapter init — do not encode None-handling in the LaTeX.
pcg_algorithm_latex.latex:
% algorithm pcg
% backend taichi
% args A:matrix, b:vector, x:vector, apply_M_inv:callable, tol:scalar, maxiter:scalar

% type r vector
% type z vector
% type p vector
% type q vector
% type rho scalar
% type rho_new scalar
% type alpha scalar
% type beta scalar
% type pq scalar
% type r0_norm scalar
% type r_norm scalar

\begin{algorithmic}
\State $r = b - A \cdot x$                                         % vector
\State $r_0 = \lVert r \rVert_2$                                    % scalar
\If{$r_0 = 0$}
    \Return $x, 0, 0$
\EndIf
\State $z = \text{apply\_M\_inv}(r)$                                % vector
\State $p = z$                                                      % vector
\State $\rho = r^\top z$                                            % scalar
\For{$k = 1, 2, \ldots, \text{maxiter}$}
    \State $q = A \cdot p$                                          % vector
    \State $pq = p^\top q$                                          % scalar
    \If{$|pq| < 10^{-300}$}
        \State \textbf{break}
    \EndIf
    \State $\alpha = \frac{\rho}{pq}$                               % scalar
    \State $x = x + \alpha \, p$                                    % vector
    \State $r = r - \alpha \, q$                                    % vector
    \State $r_n = \lVert r \rVert_2$                                % scalar
    \If{$r_n < \text{tol} \cdot r_0$}
        \Return $x, k, r_n$
    \EndIf
    \State $z = \text{apply\_M\_inv}(r)$                            % vector
    \State $\rho_{\text{new}} = r^\top z$                           % scalar
    \State $\beta = \frac{\rho_{\text{new}}}{\rho}$                 % scalar
    \State $p = z + \beta \, p$                                     % vector
    \State $\rho = \rho_{\text{new}}$                               % scalar
\EndFor
\Return $x, \text{maxiter}, \lVert r \rVert_2$
\end{algorithmic}
fixes_vs_original_v1: Renamed `M_inv` -> `apply_M_inv` to disambiguate from literal matrix inversion.
Replaced init `M z = r` (linear-system form) with callable `z = apply_M_inv(r)` so the precond syntax is consistent with the loop body.
Hoisted `r_0 = ||r||_2` once and switched convergence test to relative `r_n < tol * r_0`.
Added breakdown guard `|p^T q| < 1e-300 -> break` matching existing PCGSolver RuntimeWarning path.
Loop indexed `k = 1..maxiter` so `k` returns iteration count.
Return tuple is now 3-element `(x, k, r_n)` everywhere -- matches `tuple[np.ndarray, int, float]` Protocol.
